ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, C, F, B are on the same horizontal line, A, D, F are on the same vertical line, and there is a right-angle mark at F, indicating that AF is perpendicular to CB. In the left right triangle ACF, the hypotenuse AC is labeled 20, the base CF is labeled 12, and angle ACF is labeled 22°. In the right right triangle DBF, the hypotenuse DB is labeled 2x+1, the base FB is labeled 2x-1, and angle DBF is labeled 22°. The problem asks to find DB. Reasoning: Triangle ACF and triangle DBF are both right triangles, and each has a 22° acute angle, so they are AA similar. The correspondence is that hypotenuse AC corresponds to DB, and base CF corresponds to FB, therefore AC/CF = DB/FB. Substituting the labeled lengths gives 20/12 = (2x+1)/(2x-1). Simplifying gives 5/3 = (2x+1)/(2x-1), cross-multiplying: 5(2x-1)=3(2x+1), that is, 10x-5=6x+3, so 4x=8, x=2. Thus DB=2x+1=2(2)+1=5.
